summary:
Closed the loop on the executed experiment and corrected one of my own premises.

Confirmed defect (interpretation tied to experiment ce1a7dcb68b449448fdee06b3eb7737e-experiment, receipt 8248101f2e7e47ecae3104f94cd0357b, completed/exit 0): the receiver side of a leadership-transfer order is unbound authority. The receipt's parsed events show steady state (leader a6e1bccd… Leader term 2, target server-0967aefd… Follower term 2), the control from a non-member claimed sender with an older term changing nothing (index 2: granted false, target_moved false, comparison_index 0 holds with admission at index 1), and then one TimeoutNow from that same claimed sender moving the follower to Leader at term 3 and deposing the serving leader (index 4: target_moved true, leader_deposed true, comparison_indices 1 and 2 hold with admission at index 3). Source explains the mechanism: timeoutNow transitions unconditionally (raft.go:2209-2214), TimeoutNowRequest has only an RPCHeader and no term (commands.go:206-208), the flag skips pre-vote (raft.go:285-308) and makes voters skip the known-leader rejection (raft.go:1603-1656). Question-0 is now explained; no safety violation is claimed.

Correction of my earlier suspicion (question-1 now paused with resume conditions, gap-1 answered honestly): configuration entries never reach FSM.Apply (fsm.go:105-118) and MockFSM records only LogCommand payloads (testing.go:76-81), so the captured helper's EnsureSame comparison (testing.go:614-676) cannot show that a peer holds a configuration entry — my earlier inference that a stale-latest node had applied it was unfounded. Instrumented replay converged within 250 ms every run, and the appendEntries truncation path re-applies configuration entries in the same call (raft.go:1504-1560), so the named candidate mechanism is refuted; the >5 s mismatch remains an unexplained lag observation, with no execution requested for it.

Also recorded a source-answered negative result: the AddNonvoter asymmetry is the documented contract (api.go:959-963, configuration.go:256-276, configuration_test.go:195-202) — DemoteVoter owns vote removal — so it is not a defect. Validation of these bytes returns valid:true. The prior receipt and the earlier update.json are left untouched.
